#         # error-prov-dual-netty-spring-001

        **Suite:** customer_escalation | **Type:** error_provenance | **Difficulty:** expert
        **Repos:** netty + spring-framework

        ## Context

        A Spring WebFlux application is experiencing intermittent connection
reset errors. The errors originate in Netty's channel pipeline but
surface as generic 500 errors in Spring WebFlux.

Your task:
1. Find how Netty handles channel pipeline exceptions
2. Find how Spring WebFlux wraps Netty's reactor-netty in its server
3. Trace an exception from Netty's channel handler through reactor-netty
   into Spring WebFlux's error handling
4. Identify where error context is lost in the translation

Write your analysis to /workspace/analysis/IMPACT_REPORT.md

        ## Expected Output

        Write your analysis to `/workspace/analysis/IMPACT_REPORT.md`.

        Your report should include:
        - File paths from each repository that are relevant
        - Specific code symbols, functions, or types involved
        - The nature of each change (removal, rename, signature change, behavioral)
        - Migration recommendations

        ## Hints

        - All repos are cloned under `/workspace/`
        - Focus on import/dependency declarations first, then trace into implementation
        - Check version constraints in dependency manifests (Cargo.toml, go.mod, pom.xml, requirements.txt)


Search only these repositories: github.com/sg-evals/netty--netty-4.1.100.Final, github.com/sg-evals/spring-framework--v6.0.11

The report is written. Here is the full analysis inline:

---

## Analysis: Connection Reset Error Provenance — Netty + Spring WebFlux

### 1. Netty Channel Pipeline Exception Handling

All exceptions enter via [`DefaultChannelPipeline.fireExceptionCaught`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/netty--netty-4.1.100.Final/-/blob/transport/src/main/java/io/netty/channel/DefaultChannelPipeline.java?L905-L909), which delegates immediately to [`AbstractChannelHandlerContext.invokeExceptionCaught(head, cause)`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/netty--netty-4.1.100.Final/-/blob/transport/src/main/java/io/netty/channel/AbstractChannelHandlerContext.java?L321-L341).

The propagation is:

```
fireExceptionCaught(cause)  [DefaultChannelPipeline L906]
  → invokeExceptionCaught(head, cause)  [AbstractChannelHandlerContext L321]
      → (thread check, dispatch to event loop if needed)
      → handler().exceptionCaught(ctx, cause)  [AbstractChannelHandlerContext L343]

Default handler (ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter):
  exceptionCaught() is marked @Skip [L138]
  → ctx.fireExceptionCaught(cause)   [L143]  // forwards to next

If no handler intercepts:
  → TailContext.exceptionCaught()  [DefaultChannelPipeline L1290]
      → onUnhandledInboundException(cause)  [L1150]
          → logger.warn(...)
          → ReferenceCountUtil.release(cause)   ← EXCEPTION SILENTLY DROPPED
```

The `@Skip` annotation on [`ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter.exceptionCaught`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/netty--netty-4.1.100.Final/-/blob/transport/src/main/java/io/netty/channel/ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter.java?L138-L144) means `findContextInbound(MASK_EXCEPTION_CAUGHT)` skips every handler that does not override the method, so exceptions can leap past most of the pipeline to reach `TailContext`. At the tail, [`onUnhandledInboundException`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/netty--netty-4.1.100.Final/-/blob/transport/src/main/java/io/netty/channel/DefaultChannelPipeline.java?L1146-L1159) only logs a WARN and releases the cause — **no reactor stream signal, no channel close, exception gone**.

---

### 2. Spring WebFlux Wrapping of Reactor-Netty

The integration boundary is [`ReactorHttpHandlerAdapter`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-framework--v6.0.11/-/blob/spring-web/src/main/java/org/springframework/http/server/reactive/ReactorHttpHandlerAdapter.java) — a `BiFunction<HttpServerRequest, HttpServerResponse, Mono<Void>>` installed directly by reactor-netty's `HttpServer.handle(...)`.

Its [`apply()` method](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-framework--v6.0.11/-/blob/spring-web/src/main/java/org/springframework/http/server/reactive/ReactorHttpHandlerAdapter.java?L55-L67):

```java
return this.httpHandler.handle(request, response)
    .doOnError(ex -> logger.trace(request.getLogPrefix() + "Failed to complete: " + ex.getMessage()))
    .doOnSuccess(aVoid -> logger.trace(request.getLogPrefix() + "Handling completed"));
```

`doOnError` is a **side-effect only** — no wrapping, no metadata attached, no recovery. The raw `IOException` flows unchanged to `HttpWebHandlerAdapter`.

[`ReactorServerHttpRequest.getBody()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-framework--v6.0.11/-/blob/spring-web/src/main/java/org/springframework/http/server/reactive/ReactorServerHttpRequest.java?L113-L116) exposes Netty channel errors via `request.receive().retain().map(bufferFactory::wrap)`. If the Netty tail's `ReferenceCountUtil.release` has already freed the `ByteBuf`, a secondary `IllegalReferenceCountException` surfaces here, masking the root cause.

---

### 3. Tracing an Exception End-to-End

```
[Netty I/O thread]
OS: connection reset
→ DefaultChannelPipeline.fireExceptionCaught(IOException)         [L906]
→ invokeExceptionCaught(head, ex)                                 [L321]
→ reactor-netty's HttpTrafficHandler.exceptionCaught()            [out-of-scope]
   IF intercepted → emits onError(IOException) on request Flux
   IF NOT intercepted (@Skip bypass) → TailContext → DROPPED      [L1150]

[Reactor event loop — assuming signal was emitted]
→ ReactorServerHttpRequest.getBody() Flux: onError(IOException)   [L114]
→ ReactorHttpHandlerAdapter.apply(): doOnError TRACE only         [L66]
→ HttpWebHandlerAdapter.handle(): .onErrorResume(handleUnresolvedError)  [L249]
→ handleUnresolvedError()                                         [L284]
   response.setStatusCode(500) succeeds
     → ERROR log "500 Server Error"                               [L293]
     → return Mono.empty()  ← 500 written to a dead connection
   OR response already committed:
     → ERROR log + Mono.error(ex) → reactor-netty closes channel  [L308]
```

---

### 4. Where Error Context Is Lost

| # | Location | Nature | Consequence |
|---|----------|--------|-------------|
| **1** | [`DefaultChannelPipeline.onUnhandledInboundException` L1150](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/netty--netty-4.1.100.Final/-/blob/transport/src/main/java/io/netty/channel/DefaultChannelPipeline.java?L1150) | Behavioral — exception discarded | Exception never reaches Spring at all if not intercepted |
| **2** | [`ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter.exceptionCaught` @Skip L138](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/netty--netty-4.1.100.Final/-/blob/transport/src/main/java/io/netty/channel/ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter.java?L138) | Behavioral — handlers bypassed silently | Exceptions jump past non-overriding pipeline stages |
| **3** | [`ReactorHttpHandlerAdapter.apply()` L66](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-framework--v6.0.11/-/blob/spring-web/src/main/java/org/springframework/http/server/reactive/ReactorHttpHandlerAdapter.java?L66) | Missing enrichment | No channel ID, remote address, or handler name attached to Throwable |
| **4** | [`HttpWebHandlerAdapter.isDisconnectedClientError()` L314](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-framework--v6.0.11/-/blob/spring-web/src/main/java/org/springframework/web/server/adapter/HttpWebHandlerAdapter.java?L314) | Brittle string-match | Windows messages (`"forcibly closed"`) and non-English locales not recognized |
| **5** | [`DISCONNECTED_CLIENT_EXCEPTIONS` L72](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-framework--v6.0.11/-/blob/spring-web/src/main/java/org/springframework/web/server/adapter/HttpWebHandlerAdapter.java?L72) | Incomplete class set | `IOException` absent; only Servlet/SockJS class names listed |
| **6** | [`ReactorServerHttpRequest.getBody()` L114](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/spring-framework--v6.0.11/-/blob/spring-web/src/main/java/org/springframework/http/server/reactive/ReactorServerHttpRequest.java?L114) | Secondary error risk | Released `ByteBuf` causes misleading NPE masking the root cause |

The most actionable loss point is **#4/#5**: `isDisconnectedClientError` will not match a Netty-originated `IOException: Connection reset by peer` on Windows (wrong message string) and will not match it by class name either (only Servlet/SockJS names in the set). The result is that every client-initiated reset is logged at ERROR level as a 500, flooding logs and obscuring real server errors.

---

### 5. Migration Recommendations

**Netty:** Add an explicit `exceptionCaught`-overriding handler at the end of your `ChannelInitializer` to enrich and forward exceptions before they reach `TailContext`:

```java
pipeline.addLast("exceptionBridge", new ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter() {
    @Override
    public void exceptionCaught(ChannelHandlerContext ctx, Throwable cause) {
        // Annotate with channel metadata so Spring can log it
        ctx.fireExceptionCaught(new IOException(
            "Channel " + ctx.channel().id() + " remote=" + ctx.channel().remoteAddress(), cause));
        ctx.close();
    }
});
```

**Spring WebFlux — fix `isDisconnectedClientError`** to cover Windows and cover bare `IOException`:

```java
if (cause instanceof IOException) {
    String text = cause.getMessage() != null ? cause.getMessage().toLowerCase() : "";
    return text.contains("broken pipe") || text.contains("connection reset")
        || text.contains("forcibly closed") || text.contains("connection aborted");
}
```

**Spring WebFlux — enrich in `ReactorHttpHandlerAdapter`** using `.onErrorMap` instead of `doOnError` so downstream handlers see a wrapped exception with request metadata:

```java
return this.httpHandler.handle(request, response)
    .onErrorMap(IOException.class, ex ->
        new ReactorNettyChannelException(request.getLogPrefix(), ex));
```

**Immediate diagnostic:** enable TRACE on `org.springframework.web.server.DisconnectedClient` and DEBUG on `HttpWebHandlerAdapter` to distinguish genuine 500s from connection resets without a code change.
